source_metadata.title: Efficacy and Safety of Intrathecal Pemetrexed Combined With Dexamethasone for Treating Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Failed Leptomeningeal Metastases From EGFR-Mutant NSCLC—a Prospective, Open-Label, Single-Arm Phase 1/2 Clinical Trial (Unique Identifier: ChiCTR1800016615)

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to determine the maximum tolerated and recommended intrathecal pemetrexed doses and evaluate efficacy and safety in EGFR-mutant NSCLC leptomeningeal metastases after TKI failure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Therefore, we designed this phase 1/2 research to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the recommended dose (RD) of IP and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IP for treating LM from NSCLC.

atoms.canonical_statement: This was an open-label, single-arm phase 1/2 study conducted in China and registered as ChiCTR1800016615.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This open-label, single-arm, phase 1/2 study was carried out in the People’s Republic of China and is registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn, unique identifier: ChiCTR1800016615).

atoms.canonical_statement: The phase 2 primary endpoint was clinical response rate among patients who received at least one treatment cycle.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary end point was treatment efficacy measured as the clinical response rate in patients who had received at least one cycle of therapy.

outcome.definition: Clinical response rate in patients who received at least one cycle of therapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: Overall survival and adverse events were secondary endpoints.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Overall survival (OS) and adverse events (AEs) were evaluated as secondary end points.

outcome.definition: Overall survival and adverse events were secondary endpoints.

atoms.canonical_statement: Phase 1 used accelerated titration with single-patient cohorts until a DLT occurred at a dose level or dose level 4 was reached, after which escalation reverted to a conventional 3+3 design.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A single-patient cohort per dose level was enrolled in the accelerated dose-escalation phase, until one dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) was observed during one dose level or until dose level 4 was reached. At this dose level, the cohort was expanded to three patients and dose escalation reverted to a conventional 3 plus 3 escalation design.

atoms.canonical_statement: The recommended phase 2 dose was defined as the dose level immediately below the toxic dose level.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The RD for phase 2 trials was defined as the dose level just below this toxic dose level.

atoms.canonical_statement: The maximum tolerated dose was defined as the highest dose level at which 33% or fewer patients experienced DLTs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The MTD was defined as the highest dose level at which less than or equal to 33% of patients experienced DLTs.

atoms.canonical_statement: A DLT included grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: grade greater than or equal to 3 neurotoxicity

atoms.canonical_statement: A DLT included grade 3 or higher leukoencephalopathy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: grade greater than or equal to 3 leukoencephalopathy

atoms.canonical_statement: A DLT included grade 4 myelosuppression lasting more than 7 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: grade 4 for more than 7 days myelosuppression

atoms.canonical_statement: Phase 2 intrathecal pemetrexed was given twice during week 1 (days 1 and 5), then every 3 weeks as consolidation until progression, then every 4 weeks as maintenance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: all eligible patients received IP twice per week for one week (day 1 and day 5) as induction treatment, followed by once every 3 weeks as consolidation therapy until progressive disease (PD) was observed, and then once every 4 weeks as maintenance therapy.

exposures.frequency: days 1 and 5 for week 1, then every 3 weeks, then every 4 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients received folic acid 400 micrograms orally once daily and vitamin B12 1000 micrograms intramuscularly 1 to 2 weeks before first pemetrexed and every 9 weeks during treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All patients received supplemental folic acid (400 μg, once daily, orally) and vitamin B12 (1000 μg, intramuscular injection 1 to 2 weeks before the first dose of pemetrexed and repeated every 9 wk) during the entire treatment period

exposures.frequency: 1-2 weeks before first dose and every 9 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Dexamethasone 5 mg was administered intrathecally with each intrathecal pemetrexed dose to reduce chemical myelitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dexamethasone (5 mg, 2 mL) was administered by intrathecal injection combined with pemetrexed during each IP to reduce the incidence of chemical myelitis.

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinical response was defined by sustained complete, obvious, or partial response for at least 1 week; stable disease and progressive disease were considered ineffective.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Clinical response was defined as the continuous presence of CR, obvious response, or PR within an interval of at least 1 week. Stable disease and PD were defined as ineffective.

atoms.canonical_statement: The planned sample size was 27, designed to detect an increase in clinical response from 40% to 80% with approximately 80% power, one-sided alpha 0.20, and 10% exclusion allowance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we planned to detect an improvement in clinical response rate from 40% (on the basis of a previous study) to 80% with approximately 80% power using the Pearson chi-square test at a one-sided significance level of 0.20, assuming a 10% exclusion rate. The planned sample size was 27 patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined complete response using both neurologic findings and KPS criteria: Almost normal neurological examination; mild cranial nerve symptoms may remain; GCS 15; KPS at least 90.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Complete response | Almost normal neurological examination. Mild cranial nerve symptoms including tinnitus or blurred vision may exist. GCS score of 15. | ≥90

outcome.definition: Almost normal neurological examination; mild cranial nerve symptoms may remain; GCS 15; KPS at least 90.
outcome.measurement_method: Neurological symptoms/signs plus KPS; both conditions required synchronously

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined obvious response using both neurologic findings and KPS criteria: Significant neurologic improvement without severe symptoms/signs; GCS at least 12; KPS at least 70 or increase of 30 from baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Obvious response | Significant neurologic improvement. No severe symptoms/signs, such as severe headache, somnolence, mental status. Dizziness, confusion, mild headache, cranial nerve paralysis or radiculitis may exist. GCS≥12. | ≥70 or elevation of 30 compared with the base line level.

outcome.definition: Significant neurologic improvement without severe symptoms/signs; GCS at least 12; KPS at least 70 or increase of 30 from baseline.
outcome.measurement_method: Neurological symptoms/signs plus KPS; both conditions required synchronously

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined partial response using both neurologic findings and KPS criteria: Partial neurologic improvement with mild/moderate symptoms; GCS at least 9; KPS 50-70 or increase of 10-20 from baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Partial response | Partial neurological improvement. Still with headache or other mild/moderate symptoms/signs. GCS≥9. | 50–70 or elevation of 10–20 compared with the base line level.

outcome.definition: Partial neurologic improvement with mild/moderate symptoms; GCS at least 9; KPS 50-70 or increase of 10-20 from baseline.
outcome.measurement_method: Neurological symptoms/signs plus KPS; both conditions required synchronously

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined stable disease using both neurologic findings and KPS criteria: No visible neurologic improvement with KPS increase of 10 from baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Stable disease | No visible neurological improvement. | Elevation of 10 compared with the base line level.

outcome.definition: No visible neurologic improvement with KPS increase of 10 from baseline.
outcome.measurement_method: Neurological symptoms/signs plus KPS; both conditions required synchronously

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined progressive disease using both neurologic findings and KPS criteria: Deteriorating neurologic symptoms/signs with decreased KPS from baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Progressive disease | Deteriorative neurological symptoms and signs. | Decrease of KPS compared to the baseline level.

outcome.definition: Deteriorating neurologic symptoms/signs with decreased KPS from baseline.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study enrolled only 33 patients overall, and the authors stated that the small sample could affect statistical analyses, especially subgroup analyses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the enrolled case number was only 33. Therefore, although we confirmed the efficacy of IP in NSCLC-LM, we were unable to determine the optimal number of treatment cycles and treatment intervals and the small number of patients may affect statistical analysis especially in subgroup analysis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that intrathecal pemetrexed was effective for EGFR-mutant NSCLC leptomeningeal metastases with tolerable adverse effects and that 50 mg was an appropriate dose with few adverse effects and a promising response rate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In conclusion, our study revealed that IP is an effective treatment for LM in RGFR-mutant patients with NSCLC with tolerable side effects and that 50 mg is an appropriate dose with few adverse effects and a promising response rate.
